```{r setup-and-import}

# --- Load ALL necessary libraries ---
library(phyloseq)
library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)
library(DESeq2)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(indicspecies)
library(FSA) # For Dunn's Test
library(tidyverse) # For data manipulation

# --- Read OTU Table ---
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")


otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]


rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 


otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)


otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)
# --- Read and Process Taxonomy ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", sep = "\t", header = TRUE, quote = "")
taxonomy_clean <- lapply(strsplit(tax_raw$Taxonomy, ";"), function(x) {
    x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)|\\\"", "", x[nchar(x) > 0]); trimws(x)
})
max_ranks <- 7; taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, `length<-`, max_ranks))
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- tax_raw$OTU
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Read and Process NEW Metadata (kohlerrr.design) ---
metadata <- read.table("kohler.design.txt", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")
colnames(metadata)[2:3] <- c("SampleType", "Age")
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID
metadata <- metadata[, -1] 
metadata$SampleType <- factor(metadata$SampleType)
metadata$Feed <- factor(metadata$Feed)
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(metadata)
```

```{r phyloseq-object}

# Read OTU table
otu_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.subsample.shared", header = TRUE, sep = "\t")

# Set rownames of the matrix (Taxa) before transposing
# The original row names are NOT needed as they are just row numbers.

# Extract only the count data columns (from column 4 onwards)
otu_mat <- otu_raw[, -(1:3)]

# CRITICAL: Set the row names of the matrix (these are the sample IDs)
# This MUST be done before transposing
rownames(otu_mat) <- otu_raw$Group 

# Transpose the matrix so OTUs are rows and Samples are columns
# Now, otu_mat has OTUs as rows (OTU IDs) and Samples as columns (Sample IDs)
otu_mat <- t(otu_mat)

# Create phyloseq OTU table
# taxa_are_rows = TRUE is correct after the transpose
otu_tab <- otu_table(otu_mat, taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# Check the result
head(otu_tab)
# Read and Process Taxonomy

```

```{r}
# --- 1. Read the taxonomy file ---
tax_raw <- read.table("kohler.opti_mcc.0.03.cons.taxonomy", 
                      sep = "\t", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, quote = "")

# --- 2. Extract taxonomy strings and OTU IDs ---
taxonomy_strings <- tax_raw$Taxonomy
names(taxonomy_strings) <- tax_raw$OTU

# --- 3. Split taxonomy strings by ';' and clean ---
taxonomy_clean <- strsplit(taxonomy_strings, ";")

taxonomy_clean <- lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  x <- x[nchar(x) > 0]                # Remove empty strings
  x <- gsub("\\(.*?\\)", "", x)       # Remove confidence scores in parentheses
  x <- gsub('\\"', '', x)              # Remove escaped quotes
  trimws(x)                           # Trim whitespace
})

# --- 4. Pad each taxonomy vector to length 7 (Kingdom to Species) ---
max_ranks <- 7
taxonomy_mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(taxonomy_clean, function(x) {
  length(x) <- max_ranks  # pad with NAs if needed
  x
}))

# --- 5. Assign column and row names ---
colnames(taxonomy_mat) <- c("Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species")
rownames(taxonomy_mat) <- names(taxonomy_strings)

# --- 6. Create tax_table object for phyloseq ---
tax_tab <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_mat))

# --- Optional: Check the result ---
head(tax_tab)
```


```{r metadata-read-final}

# Load the phyloseq package
library(phyloseq)

# 1. Read the design file using the ROBUST separator sep=""
# sep="" tells R to use one or more whitespace characters (tabs/spaces) as a delimiter.
metadata <- read.table("Kohler.design", header = TRUE, sep = "", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Check the column names to verify the read
# print(colnames(metadata)) 

# 2. Rename columns for clarity and consistency (5 columns should be read now)
# Index 2: Mother -> MotherID
colnames(metadata)[2] <- "MotherID"

# Index 5: Feed -> FeedStatus
colnames(metadata)[5] <- "FeedStatus" 

# 3. Set rownames using the SampleID
rownames(metadata) <- metadata$SampleID

# 4. Prepare for phyloseq
metadata <- metadata[, -1] # Remove the redundant SampleID column

# 5. Ensure categorical variables are factors
metadata$Age <- factor(metadata$Age)
metadata$SampleType <- factor(metadata$SampleType)
metadata$FeedStatus <- factor(metadata$FeedStatus)
metadata$MotherID <- factor(metadata$MotherID)

# 6. Create the phyloseq 'sample_data' object
sample_data_obj <- sample_data(metadata)

head(sample_data_obj)
```

```{r phyloseq-object-final}

# Load necessary library
library(phyloseq)

# --- Ensure components are named for pruning ---

# Get sample names from the metadata object (which is assumed to be correct now)
meta_samples <- sample_names(sample_data_obj)

# --- Prune OTU and Tax tables to match metadata ---
# This step ensures that all components have identical sample names and counts.
otu_tab_pruned <- prune_samples(meta_samples, otu_tab)
tax_tab_pruned <- prune_taxa(taxa_names(otu_tab_pruned), tax_tab)

# --- Combine components ---
# Note: If you have a phylogenetic tree object (e.g., 'tree_obj'), add it here.
physeq <- phyloseq(otu_tab_pruned, tax_tab_pruned, sample_data_obj)

# Check the final object
print(physeq)
```


```{r data-prep-alpha-data}
# 1. Filter and Rarefy (Creates physeq_rarefied)
physeq_filt <- filter_taxa(physeq, function(x) sum(x > 3) > (0.2 * length(x)), TRUE)
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(physeq_filt)); set.seed(42)
physeq_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(physeq_filt, sample.size = min_depth, replace = FALSE)

# 2. Calculate Diversity (Creates alpha_diversity_rarefied)
alpha_diversity_rarefied <- estimate_richness(physeq_rarefied, measures = c("Observed", "Shannon"))

# 3. Merge Diversity and Metadata (Creates alpha_data_rarefied)
sample_metadata_rarefied <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_rarefied))
alpha_data_rarefied <- cbind(alpha_diversity_rarefied, sample_metadata_rarefied) 

# 4. Order Factors (Crucial for correct plotting order)
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+days", "15+days", "20+days")
alpha_data_rarefied$Age <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Age, levels = age_order)
alpha_data_rarefied$SampleType <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$SampleType, 
                                           levels = c("Mother", "Fetus", "Newborn", "7+days", "15+days", "20+days"))

```

```{r alpha-tests}
# Kruskal-Wallis Test on Shannon by Age and Feed Status

# Fix 1: The 'Age' factor needs to be applied to the current data frame first, 
# as the data was just read with the column name 'Age'.
alpha_data_rarefied$Age <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Age, levels = age_order)


kw_test_age <- kruskal.test(Shannon ~ Age, data = alpha_data_rarefied)

# Fix 2: Change 'Feed' to the correct variable name, 'FeedStatus'.
kw_test_feed <- kruskal.test(Shannon ~ FeedStatus, data = alpha_data_rarefied) 
#                             ^^^^^^^^ Corrected variable name

print(kw_test_age)
print(kw_test_feed)
```

```{r beta-tests}
bray_curtis_dist <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_rarefied, method = "bray")

# PERMANOVA for Feed Status and Full Model
permanova_result_feed <- adonis2(bray_curtis_dist ~ FeedStatus, 
                                 data = as(sample_data(physeq_rarefied), "data.frame"), permutations = 999)
permanova_result_full <- adonis2(bray_curtis_dist ~ SampleType + Age + FeedStatus, 
                                 data = as(sample_data(physeq_rarefied), "data.frame"), permutations = 999)

print("PERMANOVA Result (Feed Status):"); print(permanova_result_feed)
print("PERMANOVA Result (Full Model):"); print(permanova_result_full)

# PERMDISP for Feed Status
dispersion_feed <- betadisper(bray_curtis_dist, sample_data(physeq_rarefied)$Feed)
print("PERMDISP for Feed Status:"); anova(dispersion_feed)
```

```{r spearman-analysis-and-plot}
# Load necessary libraries (already loaded, but ensures all functions are available)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyverse) 

# --- 1. Variable Creation (Permanent Assignment without pipes) ---

# A. Clean the categorical Age column
alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned <- trimws(
    gsub(" ", "", as.character(alpha_data_rarefied$Age))
)

# B. Create the Age_Numerical column using case_when
# This ensures the output column is strictly numerical and permanently assigned.
alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Numerical <- case_when(
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned == "Fetus" ~ 0,
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned == "Newborn" ~ 1,
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned == "7+days" ~ 7,
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned == "15+days" ~ 15,
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Cleaned == "20+days" ~ 20,
    TRUE ~ NA_real_ 
)


# --- 2. Statistical Test (Optional, but included for completeness) ---
spearman_test <- cor.test(
    alpha_data_rarefied$Age_Numerical, 
    alpha_data_rarefied$Shannon, 
    method = "spearman"
)
print("Spearman Rank Correlation (Age vs. Shannon):")
print(spearman_test)

# --- 3. PLOT CREATION (Uses the guaranteed variables) ---

p_trend <- ggplot(alpha_data_rarefied, aes(x = Age_Numerical, y = Shannon)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = Age), size = 3) +
    geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "black", se = TRUE) +
    
    labs(
        title = "Microbial Shannon Diversity Trend Over Early Life Stages",
        x = "Approximate Age (Days)",
        y = "Shannon Diversity Index"
    ) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(p_trend)
```

```{r permanova-motherid}
# Load vegan (for adonis2)
library(vegan)

# Assuming bray_curtis_dist and physeq_rarefied are defined

# PERMANOVA test for Maternal ID (clutch effect)
permanova_result_mother <- adonis2(
    bray_curtis_dist ~ MotherID,
    data = as(sample_data(physeq_rarefied), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999
)

print("PERMANOVA Result (MotherID):")
print(permanova_result_mother)

# PERMDISP test for MotherID
dispersion_mother <- betadisper(bray_curtis_dist, sample_data(physeq_rarefied)$MotherID)
print("PERMDISP for MotherID:"); anova(dispersion_mother)
```

```{r plot-within-mother-dispersion}

    MotherID = sample_data(physeq_rarefied)$MotherID,
```

```{r combined-env-feed-analysis}
library(vegan)
library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)

# --- 1. Filter the phyloseq object to only include Muck and Sterile samples ---
physeq_env_subset <- subset_samples(physeq_rarefied, SampleType %in% c("Sterile", "Muck"))

# Remove groups/levels that no longer exist (e.g., "Newborn")
physeq_env_subset <- physeq_env_subset %>%
    prune_taxa(taxa_sums(.) > 0, .) %>%
    prune_samples(sample_sums(.) > 0, .)

# Ensure factor levels are correct after subsetting
physeq_env_subset@sam_data$MotherID <- droplevels(physeq_env_subset@sam_data$MotherID)


# --- 2. Calculate Distance and Run PERMANOVA (Sequential Model) ---
bray_env_subset <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_env_subset, method = "bray")

# Sequential Model: MotherID is tested first (as a confounder), 
# followed by the two environmental factors (SampleType and FeedStatus).
permanova_full_env <- adonis2(
    bray_env_subset ~ MotherID + SampleType + FeedStatus,
    data = as(sample_data(physeq_env_subset), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999
)

print("PERMANOVA Result (MotherID + SampleType + FeedStatus):")
print(permanova_full_env)
```


```{r visualize-combined-env}

library(ggplot2)
library(vegan)

# Calculate Bray–Curtis distance (if not already done)
bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_env_subset, method = "bray")

# Perform NMDS (non-metric multidimensional scaling)
nmds <- ordinate(physeq_env_subset, method = "NMDS", distance = bray_dist)

# Convert to data frame for ggplot

# Plot, coloring by a variable of interest
ggplot(nmds_df, aes(x = NMDS1, y = NMDS2, color = SampleType, shape = FeedStatus)) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = SampleType), linetype = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "NMDS Ordination (Bray–Curtis) - Colored by Sample Type",
    subtitle = "PERMANOVA significant (p = 0.001)",
    x = "NMDS1",
    y = "NMDS2"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

```

```{r permanova-variance-explained-plot}
# Example PERMANOVA result object
permanova_res <- adonis2(
  bray_env_subset ~ MotherID + SampleType + FeedStatus,
  data = as(sample_data(physeq_env_subset), "data.frame"),
  permutations = 999
)

# Convert to data frame
permanova_df <- as.data.frame(permanova_res)
permanova_df$Variable <- rownames(permanova_df)
permanova_df <- permanova_df[permanova_df$Variable != "Total", ]  # remove total row

# Plot R² (variance explained)
ggplot(permanova_df, aes(x = reorder(Variable, R2), y = R2, fill = Variable)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(
    title = "PERMANOVA Variance Explained (Bray–Curtis)",
    x = "Variable",
    y = "R² (Proportion of Variation Explained)"
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r elegant-pcoa-permanova-plots}
# Load needed libraries
library(phyloseq)
library(vegan)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis) # for better color palettes

# ----- 1. Compute Bray–Curtis distance and PCoA -----
bray_dist <- phyloseq::distance(physeq_env_subset, method = "bray")
pcoa <- ordinate(physeq_env_subset, method = "PCoA", distance = bray_dist)
pcoa_df <- plot_ordination(physeq_env_subset, pcoa, justDF = TRUE)


# ----- 4. Elegant PCoA plot -----
p1 <- ggplot(pcoa_df, aes(x = Axis.1, y = Axis.2)) +
  geom_point(aes(color = SampleType, shape = FeedStatus), size = 4, alpha = 0.8) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(group = SampleType, color = SampleType), 
               linetype = 2, linewidth = 0.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_viridis(discrete = TRUE, option = "D") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "PCoA Ordination (Bray–Curtis Distance)",
    subtitle = paste0("PERMANOVA: R² = ",
                      round(sum(permanova_df$R2), 2),
                      ", p = ",
                      format(permanova_res$`Pr(>F)`[1], digits = 3)),
    x = paste0("PCoA1 (", round(pcoa$values$Relative_eig[1] * 100, 1), "%)"),
    y = paste0("PCoA2 (", round(pcoa$values$Relative_eig[2] * 100, 1), "%)")
  )

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(viridis)

# Convert adonis2 result to a data frame
permanova_df <- as.data.frame(
  adonis2(
    bray_dist ~ MotherID + SampleType + FeedStatus,
    data = as(sample_data(physeq_env_subset), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999,
    by = "margin"
  )
)

# Add a variable column
permanova_df$Variable <- rownames(permanova_df)

# Clean it up: remove residuals, totals, and zero-variance variables
permanova_df <- permanova_df %>%
  filter(!(Variable %in% c("Residual", "Total"))) %>%
  filter(R2 > 0) %>%
  mutate(
    Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable[order(R2, decreasing = TRUE)]),
    perc = round(R2 * 100, 1)
  )

# --- Plot ---
p2 <- ggplot(permanova_df, aes(x = R2, y = Variable, fill = Variable)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7, color = "black") +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste0(perc, "%")),
            hjust = -0.15, size = 4.5) +
  scale_fill_viridis_d(option = "C", end = 0.85) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(permanova_df$R2) + 0.05)) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "none",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold")
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "PERMANOVA: Variance Explained by Factor",
    subtitle = "Bray–Curtis dissimilarity (999 permutations)",
    x = expression(R^2 ~ "(Proportion of Variation Explained)"),
    y = NULL
  )



# install.packages("patchwork") # if not installed
library(patchwork)
p1 + p2 + plot_layout(widths = c(2.2, 2))

```

```{r part-1-data-prep}
# Load necessary libraries (redundant, but good for self-contained chunk)
library(phyloseq)
library(tidyverse)

# --- 1. Filter and Rarefy (Creates physeq_rarefied) ---
# Filter out rare taxa
physeq_filt <- filter_taxa(physeq, function(x) sum(x > 3) > (0.2 * length(x)), TRUE)

# Rarefy to the minimum depth for robust comparison
min_depth <- min(sample_sums(physeq_filt))
set.seed(42) 
physeq_rarefied <- rarefy_even_depth(physeq_filt, sample.size = min_depth, replace = FALSE)

# --- 2. Calculate Diversity (Creates alpha_diversity_rarefied) ---
alpha_diversity_rarefied <- estimate_richness(
    physeq_rarefied, 
    measures = c("Observed", "Shannon", "Simpson")
)

# --- 3. Merge Diversity and Metadata (Creates alpha_data_rarefied) ---
sample_metadata_rarefied <- as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_rarefied))

# The final plotting data frame
alpha_data_rarefied <- cbind(alpha_diversity_rarefied, sample_metadata_rarefied) 

# --- 4. Order Factors for Plotting and Analysis ---

# A. Order the Age Factor (Crucial for correct plot order)
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+days", "15+days", "20+days")
alpha_data_rarefied$Age <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$Age, levels = age_order)

# B. Ensure FeedStatus is a factor (Critical for the K-W test)
alpha_data_rarefied$FeedStatus <- factor(alpha_data_rarefied$FeedStatus)

# C. Create the Numerical Age column for trend analysis
alpha_data_rarefied <- alpha_data_rarefied %>%
  mutate(
    Age_Cleaned = trimws(gsub(" ", "", as.character(Age))),
    Age_Numerical = case_when(
      Age_Cleaned == "Fetus" ~ 0,
      Age_Cleaned == "Newborn" ~ 1,
      Age_Cleaned == "7+days" ~ 7,
      Age_Cleaned == "15+days" ~ 15,
      Age_Cleaned == "20+days" ~ 20,
      TRUE ~ NA_real_
    )
  )

# Display head of the final data frame to confirm structure
head(alpha_data_rarefied)

print(permanova_full_env)
```

```{r plot-variance-explained}
# Convert the full sequential PERMANOVA result to a data frame
permanova_res <- adonis2(
    bray_curtis_dist ~ MotherID + FeedStatus + Age + SampleType, # Use the full set of factors
    data = as(sample_data(physeq_rarefied), "data.frame"),
    permutations = 999,
    by = "margin" # Use 'margin' to get the effect of each factor
)

permanova_df <- as.data.frame(permanova_res)
permanova_df$Variable <- rownames(permanova_df)

# Filter, calculate percentage, and order by R2
permanova_df <- permanova_df %>%
    filter(!(Variable %in% c("Residual", "Total"))) %>%
    mutate(
        Variable = gsub("MotherID", "Maternal Clutch (MotherID)", Variable),
        Variable = gsub("FeedStatus", "Feeding Status (Independent)", Variable),
        Variable = factor(Variable, levels = Variable[order(R2)]),
        R2_perc = round(R2 * 100, 1)
    )

p_r2_bar <- ggplot(permanova_df, aes(x = R2, y = Variable, fill = R2)) +
    geom_col(color = "black") +
    geom_text(aes(label = paste0(R2_perc, "%")), hjust = -0.1, size = 4) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "lightblue", high = "darkblue") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, max(permanova_df$R2) + 0.1)) +
    labs(
        title = "Fig 2. Partitioning of Community Variance (R²)",
        subtitle = "Maternal ID accounts for the largest explained fraction.",
        x = expression(R^2 ~ "(Proportion of Variation Explained)"),
        y = NULL
    ) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")

print(p_r2_bar)
```

```{r deseq2-feed-setup}

diagdds <- phyloseq_to_deseq2(physeq_deseq, ~ FeedStatus)

# Run the DESeq2 analysis (takes a moment)
diagdds <- DESeq(diagdds, test = "Wald", fitType = "parametric")
```

```{r plot-age-order-fix}

# Calculate multiple metrics
alpha_full <- estimate_richness(physeq_rarefied, 
	measures = c("Observed", "Chao1", "Shannon", "Simpson", "InvSimpson"))

# Merge with metadata
alpha_full_meta <- cbind(alpha_full, as.data.frame(sample_data(physeq_rarefied)))

# --- CRITICAL FIX: Order the Age Factor ---

# Define the full chronological order of the age categories
age_order <- c("Fetus", "Newborn", "7+days", "15+days", "20+days")

# Apply the chronological order to the Age column in the data frame
alpha_full_meta$Age <- factor(alpha_full_meta$Age, levels = age_order)

# --- Statistical tests (Now using the ordered factor) ---
kruskal.test(Shannon ~ FeedStatus, data = alpha_full_meta)
kruskal.test(Observed ~ Age, data = alpha_full_meta)

# Dunn's post-hoc test if Kruskal-Wallis is significant
library(FSA)
dunnTest(Shannon ~ Age, data = alpha_full_meta, method = "bonferroni")

# --- Visualization (Will now be in chronological order) ---
p_shannon_age_feed <- ggplot(alpha_full_meta, aes(x = Age, y = Shannon, fill = FeedStatus)) +
	geom_boxplot() +
    geom_point(position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.1, dodge.width = 0.75), alpha = 0.6) + # Add points for detail
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("No" = "#1F78B4", "Yes" = "#E31A1C")) + # Custom colors
	labs(
        title = "Shannon Diversity Across Age and Feed Status",
        subtitle = "Age is ordered chronologically",
        x = "Age Group",
        y = "Shannon Diversity Index",
        fill = "Fed Status"
    ) +
	theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

print(p_shannon_age_feed)
```

```{r}

# Subset to mother samples (if available in dataset)
# Assuming mothers are labeled in metadata
mothers <- subset_samples(physeq_rarefied, SampleType == "MotherID")
offspring <- subset_samples(physeq_rarefied, SampleType != "MotherID")

# Calculate shared OTUs between each mother and her offspring
# This requires custom code to loop through MotherID groups

library(dplyr)
shared_otus <- data.frame()

for(mom_id in unique(sample_data(offspring)$MotherID)) {
  mom_sample <- subset_samples(mothers, MotherID == mom_id)
  off_samples <- subset_samples(offspring, MotherID == mom_id)
  
  mom_otus <- taxa_names(prune_taxa(taxa_sums(mom_sample) > 0, mom_sample))
  off_otus <- taxa_names(prune_taxa(taxa_sums(off_samples) > 0, off_samples))
  
  shared <- length(intersect(mom_otus, off_otus))
  total_off <- length(off_otus)
  
  shared_otus <- rbind(shared_otus, data.frame(
    MotherID = mom_id,
    Shared_OTUs = shared,
    Total_Offspring_OTUs = total_off,
    Percent_Shared = (shared / total_off) * 100
  ))
}

print(shared_otus)
```

```{r}
core_muck <- filter_taxa(subset_samples(physeq_rarefied, FeedStatus == "Yes"),
```
